name: Throughline
pitch: A decoupled Laravel API + React SPA for scheduling production work orders, queued to done.
description: A production-scheduling Kanban board, built the opposite shape from GreenStock on purpose: an API-only Laravel backend (no Blade, no Inertia) consumed by a fully separate React + TypeScript SPA, deployed to two different platforms and talking cross-origin over a bearer token.

highlights.title: Server-authoritative drag-and-drop
highlights.body: A dropped card sends the two cards it landed between, never a position it computed itself. The server re-reads real positions inside a transaction, computes the midpoint, and rebalances the whole column if repeated same-spot drops have halved the gap too many times to represent distinctly — so two racing tabs can never corrupt the ordering.

highlights.title: An audit trail, the second time on purpose
highlights.body: The same append-only-ledger philosophy as GreenStock's inventory_movements, applied to workflow instead of stock: every real stage change, line reassignment, or priority edit is logged. A same-column drag reorder deliberately isn't — a row saying "position moved from 1500 to 1499.9" has no audit value, so it's excluded on purpose rather than by omission.

highlights.title: A genuinely decoupled architecture
highlights.body: The API (Render) and the SPA (Vercel) know nothing about each other beyond a base URL and a CORS allow-list — no shared cookie, no shared session. Auth is a bearer token, which sidesteps Sanctum's SPA-cookie-mode configuration entirely since there's no same-site relationship to maintain.

highlights.title: CI from day one
highlights.body: GitHub Actions runs the backend PHPUnit suite plus a frontend typecheck/lint/build on every push — this project's first CI pipeline, later extended to GreenStock too. A separate job also notifies this portfolio site to rebuild whenever either project's description changes here.
